SUBJECT:  Request from Wolfgang Puck to use the City Shield for their Beverly Hills Autumn
  BBQ event marketing

ATTACHMENTS:  1. Proposed Autumn BBQ with City Shield Design
  2. Beverly Hills Autum BBQ Event Details

INTRODUCTION
The City periodically receives inquiries about the use of the trademarked Beverly Hills City Shield.
This report provides the City Council Liaison/Branding and Licensing Committee of Mayor
Sharona Nazarian, PsyD and Councilmember Mary Wells (Liaisons) with an overview of the
proposal for use of the City Shield by Wolfgang Puck for their Beverly Hills Autumn BBQ event
marketing.
The City Council Liaisons are requested to review the proposed use of the City Shield, for the
attached product design only.

DISCUSSION
Staff receives inquiries from individuals and businesses looking to use the trademarked Beverly
Hills Shield on products and merchandise. As requests are received, they are referred to the City’s
branding and licensing consultant CMG Worldwide (CMG). The City has contracted with CMG
Worldwide since 2013.
Wolfgang Puck is a renowned chef and restaurateur whose flagship restaurant, Spago Beverly
Hills, has become an iconic culinary destination since opening on Canon Drive in 1997. Originally
launched in 1982 on the Sunset Strip, Spago helped define California cuisine with its fresh,
innovative approach and celebrity clientele. The Beverly Hills location continues to showcase
seasonal menus crafted with locally sourced ingredients, earning critical acclaim and accolades
including two Michelin stars. Spago remains a cornerstone of the City’s fine dining scene.
Building on this legacy of culinary excellence, the team at Wolfgang Puck is organizing a new
elevated fundraiser titled the Beverly Hills Autumn BBQ, scheduled to take place on October 19,
2025, at Beverly Canon Gardens. This exclusive event will feature Wolfgang Puck and is expected
   Page 2

to draw 275 to 300 guests. Other celebrated chefs, including Grant Achatz, Evan Funke, and
Nancy Silverton, have been invited and are likely to attend.
The event will benefit No Kid Hungry, a national campaign dedicated to ending childhood hunger
in America. All proceeds from the silent auction, led by the No Kid Hungry team, as well as the
event’s net revenue, will be donated directly to support their mission. Guests will have the
opportunity to bid on exclusive items and experiences, with 100 percent of auction proceeds
helping ensure every child has access to the nutritious food they need to thrive.
The event will be co-presented by Spago Beverly Hills and The Maybourne, with tickets priced at
$295 per guest. It will not operate as a for-profit endeavor, and all proceeds will be directed to the
beneficiary.
As part of their branding and promotional materials, the event organizers have proposed
incorporating the City of Beverly Hills shield alongside the event title “Autumn Barbecue.” While
it is generally against City practice to alter or stylize the shield, the CMG team believes the
proposed design remains faithful to the shield’s integrity and visual identity.
Given the charitable nature of the event, the organizers are requesting a waiver of the licensing
fee traditionally associated with use of the City shield.

TO:  City Council Liaison! Branding and Licensing Committee
FROM:  Joe Evans, City Manager’s Office
DATE:  August 6, 2025
SUBJECT:  Licensing Partnership Request from Pearson Brothers Winery

ATTACHMENTS:  1. Sample High End Wooden Presentation Boxes

INTRODUCTION
The City periodically receives inquiries about the use of the trademarked Beverly Hills City Shield.
This report provides the City Council Liaison!Branding and Licensing Committee of Mayor
Sharona Nazarian, PsyD and Councilmember Mary Wells (Liaisons) with an overview of the
proposal for licensing partnership with Pearson Brothers Winery, creators of Perduret.
The City Council Liaisons are requested to review the proposed licensing partnership for
developing a custom-designed, federally approved label and packaging that incorporates the
Beverly Hills name.

DISCUSSION
Staff receives inquiries from individuals and businesses looking to use the trademarked Beverly
Hills Shield on products and merchandise. As requests are received, they are referred to the City’s
branding and licensing consultant CMG Worldwide (CMG). The City has contracted with CMG
Worldwide since 2013.
The City is currently exploring a potential branding and licensing collaboration with Pearson
Brothers Winery, known for creating Perduret, a sparkling wine made through Saccharo
winemaking, a sustainable and federally approved method that uses honey rather than grapes.
Recognized in Food & Beverage Magazine, Perduret has gained national attention for its
environmentally friendly approach, carbon-negative impact, and dedication to protecting
pollinators. The winery, located on a 63-acre wildlife preserve in San Diego, produces a one-of
a-kind, high-end product that complements Beverly Hills’ values of luxury, exclusivity, and
environmental responsibility.
The proposed partnership would involve developing a custom-designed, federally approved label
and packaging that incorporates the Beverly Hills name. There would be no upfront financial
commitment from the City. CEO Dale Pearson has proposed launching with a limited edition of
   Page 2

30 cases, or 360 bottles, priced between $330 and $340 each, packaged in premium wooden
boxes. Perduret has already been showcased at elite venues and events, including the
Maybourne Hotel, Beverly Hills Hotel, Gravitas, Beverly Hills Fashion Week, David Levine Design
Gallery, and Blvkbook Art Gallery, reflecting strong community interest.
Under the terms of the proposed agreement, the City would receive a royalty of 10 to 12 percent
of net sales. Due to the winery’s substantial investment in branding, packaging, and regulatory
approvals, an advance is not being offered. The initial release is expected to generate more than
$10,000 in royalties, with long-term potential to expand the partnership and generate annual
revenue in the six-figure range.

FISCAL IMPACT
Agreement terms including any advance and royalties will be brought back to the Liaisons for
review, as well as the duration of the agreement.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff requests that the City Council Branding and Licensing Committee review and provide
feedback regarding the proposed licensing partnership with Pearson Brothers Winery. Based on
the direction received, the proposal will return for a review of terms with Liaisons before moving
onto Council for approval.
